In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Müller and Pilzecher’s experiments have provided the first evidence that learning is not instantaneous and permanent, and have introduced the concept of memory as a process that takes time to become fixed.
the consolidation of a memory trace takes place over a time span of several days, and is completed by the end of the first week after the learning experience.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the consolidation of memory is not a simple process, but rather it is a complicated process involving a number of different brain structures, and that the process is dependent on a number of variables.
the consolidation of memory traces is a dynamic process that involves the formation, maturation, and integration of memory networks.
the memory of an impression is not a simple, unchangeable, and permanent fact but a complex and variable process that is subject to many changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown that memory consolidation can occur in the presence of an amnesic drug and in the absence of sleep, which is contrary to a prevailing view that sleep is necessary for memory consolidation.
memory consolidation is a process that takes time.
